title: Adding spaces around the part number is not a change
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Click at the start of the Part Number.
  4. Type two spaces.
  5. Click at the end of the Part Number.
  6. Type two spaces.
  7. Click Save.
  8. Click the clock icon (Part History) at the left of the part A row.
  9. Click Parts in the top bar.
  10. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  11. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  12. Click the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • The cursor is at the start of the part number.

Step 4:

  • Two spaces sit before the number.

Step 5:

  • The cursor is at the end of the part number.

Step 6:

  • Two spaces sit after the number.

Step 7:

  • The save goes through and the window closes.

Step 8:

  • Part History opens for part A, and it lists no "Part number updated" entry.

Step 9:

  • The Parts left menu shows Inventory.

Step 10:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 11:

  • Part A is listed under its number, with no spaces.

Step 12:

  • Part Number reads part A's number exactly as it was saved, with no spaces.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-N3a: “A typed number that differs from the saved one only by spaces before or after it is not a change. The saved number is kept as it is.”
